pointers.sentence: Beside it, `django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py` holds the four validators Django ships, their help texts, and `password_changed`, which tells them a password was set.

A **password validator** is an object of any class with two methods, `validate(password, user=None)`, which raises `ValidationError` to refuse, and `get_help_text()`, which states the rule; it may have a third, `password_changed(password, user=None)` (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).
It is empty by default, so a project that leaves it validates nothing (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

The settings startproject writes list Django's four without options: `UserAttributeSimilarityValidator`, `MinimumLengthValidator`, `CommonPasswordValidator`, `NumericPasswordValidator` (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`).
A failed import, a class missing from its module included, becomes `ImproperlyConfigured`, as does a name that is not callable (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:get_password_validators`).
In Django only the test framework empties the cache, when a test overrides the setting ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md)) (`django/test/signals.py:auth_password_validators_changed`).

If any refused, it raises one `ValidationError` of the list, so every reason comes at once, each with its code ([Django's exceptions: `django.core.exceptions`](../utils/exceptions.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:validate_password`).

`MinimumLengthValidator` refuses a password shorter than `min_length=8` or the options' length, with the code `"password_too_short"` (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:MinimumLengthValidator`).

`NumericPasswordValidator` refuses one made only of digits, `"password_entirely_numeric"`; it asks `str.isdigit`, which is true of other scripts' digits too (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:NumericPasswordValidator`).

The validator reads the whole file into a set when it is made, as gzip or else as plain text, and compares the password lowercased and stripped of surrounding white space, as " LIGHTHOUSE " shows (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:CommonPasswordValidator`).

At `max_similarity=0.7` or above, or the options' limit (at least 0.1), the password is refused with `"password_too_similar"` and the field's verbose name, or the attribute's name (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:UserAttributeSimilarityValidator.validate`).

A part a tenth of the password's length or less, too short to reach the limit, is not measured (at a limit of 0.2 or below, only a shorter part), which the docstring of `exceeds_maximum_length_ratio` says avoids the potentially expensive sequence matching (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:exceeds_maximum_length_ratio`).

It is wrapped by `lazy`: the password forms take it as a help text as their classes are defined, and it is built at each rendering ([Lazy values: `lazy`, `Promise` and `keep_lazy`](../utils/lazy.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:password_validators_help_text_html`, `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:SetPasswordMixin.create_password_fields`).

It is wrapped by `lazy`: the password forms take it as a help text as their classes are defined, and it is built at each rendering ([Lazy values: `lazy`, `Promise` and `keep_lazy`](../utils/lazy.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:password_validators_help_text_html`, `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:SetPasswordMixin.create_password_fields`).

`AbstractBaseUser.save`, once the row is written, hands it to `password_changed` with the user and forgets it, so the hook runs once, at the first save after a password is set, even a save that does not write the password (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.save`).
`password_changed` calls the method of that name on each validator that has one; none of Django's four has (`django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py:password_changed`).
The documentation's example is a validator refusing a password used before (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).

`AbstractBaseUser.check_password`, upgrading a hash, clears the raw password before it saves, its comment saying an upgrade is not a password change; `UserManager.create_user` hashes with `make_password`, not `set_password` (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.check_password`, `django/contrib/auth/models.py:UserManager._create_user_object`).

`BaseUserCreationForm._post_clean` asks once the form's values are on the new user, so the username being chosen is compared; `SetPasswordForm.clean` (and so `PasswordChangeForm`) and `AdminPasswordChangeForm.clean` ask too, the admin's forms only when the password is to be usable ([The authentication forms: `AuthenticationForm` and the password forms](user-forms.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:SetPasswordMixin.validate_password_for_user`, `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:SetUnusablePasswordMixin.validate_password_for_user`). createsuperuser asks only when it prompts, against an unsaved user made from the answers, and offers to go on anyway; changepassword asks whenever the two entries match, for three tries at most ([Creating a superuser: createsuperuser and changepassword](createsuperuser.md)).

The documentation gives two reasons: developers, not users, work at that level, and a model's validation does not run as it is created (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).
